title: Era-conditioned TESS CPV tests leave month-scale flag independence allowed
abstract: We test whether CPV flags cluster within stars beyond fixed stellar rates. An exact conditional success-run calculation uses 8,772 TESS sectors of 1,746 clean rapid rotators, with 245 flags. For gaps at most 60 days, fixing each stellar total gives 49 informative adjacent flagged pairs against 40.56 expected, with one-sided p=0.00807. Adding efficiency bins and separate observing eras gives 18 against 13.73, with p=0.0524. The conditional interaction is 0.777, with an exact central 95% interval of -0.143 to 1.720. Its estimate changes little while uncertainty grows. All era-conditioned 60-day intervals include independence. None of 27 exploratory tests passes a Bonferroni threshold. The evidence suggests extra clustering but does not establish a robust episode clock. The method removes arbitrary fixed stellar rate differences without fitting a duty distribution. Equal probability within strata, inherited flags, detection calibration, source selection and limited informative stars constrain the test. It measures no material lifetime. Original code, aggregate distributions, a figure and exact input hashes support repetition.

display.caption: Observed excess pairs and exact conditional interaction intervals at a 60-day maximum gap. Era controls leave zero interaction allowed.
